record_identity.title: Govern the Deployed Composition, Not the Product Label

report_title: Govern the Deployed Composition, Not the Product Label
case_descriptor: Lessons from cross-runtime governance ambiguity and the composed-system architecture refactor
summary: A common product, account, persona, model family, or conversation does not establish that the same governed system is active across every mode. Assessment must identify the incident-time deployed composition—generation, selection, arbitration, harness, agency, execution, authority, hosting, custody, embodiment, reliance, and governance stack—without collapsing unknown or distributed architecture into a single categorical label.
what_happened: During July 2026, linked observations and an OpenAI staff acknowledgment documented material divergence and memory unreliability across ChatGPT voice and runtime pathways while internal corpus reach and causal architecture remained unknown.
VIGIL identified that a shared product, account, persona, conversation, or model label could conceal materially different responding formations and unsupported cross-runtime conformance assumptions.

CAM replaced the former categorical cognition and origin ontology with a composed deployed-system architecture, incident-time attribution, architecture-change governance, and AI-ABOM foundations while external runtime conformance remains under monitoring.
governance_misconception: A product or model label was treated as a sufficient description of the governed system.
Governance behaviour observed in one runtime was treated as transferable evidence for another mode, client, router, harness, or output pathway.
A single cognition or origin category was treated as capable of carrying architecture, control, agency, execution, hosting, custody, and accountability at once.
Unknown internal architecture was treated as permission to infer a unified responding entity rather than preserve uncertainty.
abstracted_learning: Governance attaches to the deployed composition that actually produced, selected, authorised, executed, rendered, or preserved the outcome. System dimensions must remain independently evidenced and reconstructable at the relevant time; shared branding, identity continuity, or model lineage cannot substitute for runtime-specific conformance.
integrated_learning: Product identity is not deployed-system identity.
Model identity is not operational-harness identity.
Conversation or persona continuity is not proof of unchanged generation, selection, arbitration, memory, governance, or output pathways.
Architecture, agency, execution, control authority, hosting, portability, custody, embodiment dependency, and systemic reliance should be assessed independently.
Distributed, harness-mediated, unitary, and human-mediated topologies require an accountable outcome boundary without being forced into one internal-arbitration model.
Unknown architecture, initiation, authorship, causal contribution, and culpability must remain unknown until evidenced.
Material architecture change requires renewed assessment and conformance review.
risk_if_not_integrated: Failures may be attributed to the wrong model, agent, operator, harness, provider, or institution.
Governance coverage in one runtime may be falsely represented as control over another.
Distributed or human-mediated contribution may disappear behind a single model or persona label.
Incident reconstruction may preserve the current architecture rather than the formation active when the event occurred.
Deprecated categorical labels may create false certainty, incompatible validators, and governance blind spots as systems become more compositional.
future_application: Voice, text, multimodal, and agentic modes
generalisation_boundary: This lesson does not require disclosure of proprietary weights or every internal implementation detail, deny legitimate product-level identity, or presume that every mode change creates a different legal entity. It applies where materially different components, controls, pathways, or responsible actors could affect governance reach, authority, behaviour, attribution, or conformance.
